content.text: Vitamin
Vitamin B9 (Folate /Folic Acid)
Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)
Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
RDA (Adults)
Serum folate: +3 ng/mL          RBC folate (better store): +140 ng/mL
Preg: 600 µg DFE                      Lactation: 500 µg DFE
RDA: 400 µg DFE/day              UL: 1000 µg/day (synth)
Serum B12: 200–900 pg/mL (180–914 pmol/L)
Gray zone: 200–400 -check methylmalonic acid (MMA) & homocysteine
RDA: 2.4 µg/day                           No established UL
Serum ascorbate: 23–114 µmol/L
RDA:      F: 75 mg/day        M: 90 mg/day
Smokers +35 mg/day                            UL: 2000 mg/day
Food Sources
Dark green leafy veggies (spinach, asparagus, broccoli)
Legumes (lentils, beans, chickpeas), Liver, citrus fruits, avocado
Fortified grains/cereals (mandated in USA since 1998)
ONLY animal prod: meat, fish, poultry, shellfish (clams =richest source)
Dairy, eggs, fortified food (plant-based milks, nutritional yeast, breakfast cereals)
No reliable plant sources — strict vegans must supp
Citrus fruit (orange, lemon, grapefruit), broccoli, brussel sprout, tomato
Bell peppers (highest mg/g), strawberries, kiwi
Not stored in lrg amounts: daily intake essential
Absorption & Storage
- Dietary folate -> monoglutamate in gut; absorb in jejunum
- stored in liver (3–4M supply)
- Active form: THF (tetrahydrofolate): cofactor in DNA synth (1-C met),
purine & thymidine synth, AA interconversion (homocysteine ->
methionine)
- MTHFR polymorphism (C677T) impairs conversion to active methylfolate
- Requires intrinsic factor (IF) prod by gastric parietal cells for ileal absorb
- Also: passive absorb (~1%) w.o IF @ pharm doses
- stored: liver holds 2–5 yr supply (hepatic stores prevent rapid depletion)
- Active forms: methylcobalamin is cofactor for methionine synth, homocysteine
metabolism) & adenosylcobalamin is a cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA
mutase (propionate metabolism via MMA pathway)
- Absorb in sm intestine via Na-dependent active transport
- stored min; excess excreted in urine
- Saturable absorb: above ~200 mg, bioavailability ↓sharply
- Easily destroyed by heat, light & O2 (cooking ↓content)
Deficiency Effects & Causes
DEFICIENCY:
-Megaloblastic macrocytic anemia (lrg, immature RBCs:  impair DNA synth)
- Hypersegmented neutrophils on peripheral smear
- Glossitis, mouth sores
-Neural tube defect: spina bifida, anencephaly -deficient peri-conceptional
- ↑homocysteine: cardiovascular risk
- Psychiatric Sx, cog decline
Causes: poor diet (esp low veggie intake), alcoholism, preg (dramatically ↑demand), malabsorb (celiac, IBD), methotrexate & other folate antagonist drugs, phenytoin, sulfasalazine, MTHFR polymorphism
DEFICIENCY:  ↑MMA & homocysteine (confirms deficiency)
-Megaloblastic macrocytic anemia (blood smear -hypersegmented neutrophils)
- Subacute Combined Degen of Spinal Cord: demyelination of P/lat columns
-   Poss irreversible: vibration/position sense loss, spastic paraparesis, ataxia
- Periph neuropathy, Glossitis
- Psychiatric: depression, psychosis, dementia, personality chg

Causes: pernicious anemia (MCC=autoimmune destruction of parietal cells/IF), strict vegan/vegetarian diet, gastric surgery (gastrectomy, bariatric), metformin use (↓absorb), H2 blockers/PPIs (↓acid needed for absorb), ileal disease (Crohn's, ileal resection), fish tapeworm, aging (atrophic gastritis)
DEFICIENCY (Scurvy):
- Perifollicular hemorrhages, corkscrew hairs (classic early signs)
- Gum bleeding, gingivitis, loose teeth, poor wound healing, easy bruising
- Fatigue, depression, joint pain
- Impaired collagen synth: vit C=cofactor for hydroxylation of
proline/lysine in collagen
Causes: poor fruit/vegetable intake, smoke, alcoholism, elderly w restricted diets, eating dx
Toxicity (Excess) Effects & Causes
TOXICITY:
- Low inherent toxicity
- High doses can mask ↓B12 -tx megaloblastic anemia
but ⍉ neuro damage —dangerous
- poss ↑progression of existing colorectal CA or undx B12 deficiency
- UL applies to synth folic acid only (food folate has no UL)
TOXICITY:
- Extremely safe: ⍉even @very high doses
- Excess excreted renally
- No established UL
- Very rare: acneiform skin eruptions w high-dose cyanocobalamin
TOXICITY:
- Gen safe: excess excreted in urine
- High doses (>2000 mg/day): GI distress, osmotic diarrhea, nausea
- Oxalate kidney stones: ↑risk w megadoses
- Interfere w some labs: glucose oxidase method -↓or↑ glucose reading
- Iron overload risk in hemochromatosis -↑iron absorb
Supp Commonly Needed?
YES:  universal supp recommended for all AFAB childbearing age & during preg (400–800 µg/day) -> NTDs
Yes: alcoholics, pt on methotrexate/anticonvulsants & pt w malabsorb or MTHFR mut
YES: high priority for: all strict vegans/vegetarians (universal supp needed)
Yes: pernicious anemia (IM B12 inj or very high oral doses 1000+ µg)
Yes: post-bariatric surgery, metformin users (monitor Q1yr), elderly w atrophic gastritis, pt w ileal dz/resection
Rare: w adequate diet
Yes: smokers (+35 mg), wound healing, critically ill pt & pt w very restricted fruit/vegetable intake
Uses
MOA: convert -> tetrahydrofolate (THF) (coenzyme that enables
transfer of 1-C units for nucleotide synth & methylation rxn)
- crucial for DNA/RNA synth, cell division & AA metabolism
- vital to prevent neural tube defects (NTDs) during fetal develop
MOA: cofactor for two enzymes -> methionine synth &
L-methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (crucial for AA metabolism & n. health)
- DNA synth, neuro function & RBC formation
MOA: reducing agent, maintain metal ions in reduced form to enable key
enzymatic rxn
- antioxidant & enzyme cofactor: function via donating e
to maintain
collagen synth, protect cells from oxidative stress & support immune
